newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF hikes dividend but shares fall three pct.
newsitem.headline: BASF hikes dividend but shares fall three pct.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG on Tuesday followed its domestic rivals in posting higher 1996 profits but its shares fell three percent amid general disappointment in the sector's performance.
BASF said it was raising its dividend for 1996 to 1.70 marks ($1) per share from 1.40 marks and that group net profit rose 12.9 percent to 2.79 billion marks from 2.47 billion marks.
Pre-tax profit climbed 6.9 percent to 4.41 billion marks from 4.13 billion, above analysts' forecasts for a five percent rise. The dividend payout also beat forecasts for a figure of 1.60 marks.
"The dividend was a real surprise, BASF obviously wanted to match the dividend paid out by Bayer," said Ronald Koehler, chemicals analyst at BHF-Bank.

"BASF has held its ground relatively well in the difficult chemicals market but Bayer remains my favourite due to its very strong drugs business." Bayer last week announced it planned to raise its dividend to 1.70 marks per share from 1.50 marks.
BASF's results gave its shares a short-lived boost but they closed down 1.84 marks or 2.9 percent at 68.70 marks, exceeding a 1.78 percent in the DAX index of 30 leading German shares.
Other chemicals stocks also declined as the entire sector fell out of favour with investors who have become used to record performances by chemicals groups.
In 1995, Hoechst and BASF lifted their net profit by 65 percent and 92 percent respectively while Bayer reported a 20 percent gain.
Bayer AG's share price closed down 3.10 marks or 4.3 percent at 68.70 marks after the company told its annual news conference its 1997 profit would at least match the 1996 level.
Bayer last week reported a 13.5 percent rise in net profit to 2.75 billion marks.
Shares in Hoechst AG also fell, closing down 2.45 marks or 3.5 percent at 67.05 marks.

The group, Europe's largest chemicals company, last week said it planned to lift its dividend to 1.40 marks from 1.30 and posted a 23.6 percent gain in pre-tax profit to 5.28 billion marks, well below expectations for a gain of 50 percent.
Hoechst shares plummeted last week after the company disappointed investors by shelving plans to list its drugs subsidiary HMR.
